summary: A pale folded spring false morel on sandy forest litter whose focal name resolves through GBIF's Catalogue of Life workflow to the accepted species Gyromitra gigas, with Swedish records shaped as much by early-season search effort as by abundance.

Wider habitat view of several fruit bodies emerging low among sticks, litter and early spring ground flora on the forest floor.

hero.lede: Snow False Morel is easy to miss if you look at the wrong time: it fruits in the first real spring window, when last year's leaf litter still dominates the ground and only the earliest woodland herbs are up. The focal name Maublancomyces gigas now resolves in GBIF's Catalogue of Life workflow to Gyromitra gigas, and that makes it a good revisit species for two reasons at once: it teaches early-season timing, and it rewards careful comparison with stenmurkla by showing a paler, bulkier fruit body whose cap edge is usually freer from the stem.
hero.shortMorphology: Large pale tan to ochre folded false morel with thick rounded lobes, a stout whitish stem and a cap edge that is usually not fully attached to the stem.

distribution.globalSummary: GBIF resolves the focal name to the accepted species Gyromitra gigas and the filtered observation layer adds 3,350 post-2000 human or machine observations, concentrated most strongly in Russia and northern Europe. That map should still be read cautiously: recent species-complex work shows that older broad uses of the G. gigas name can mask cryptic relatives, especially outside Europe, so the open-data footprint is an observation layer rather than a clean native-range map.
distribution.swedenSummary: Sweden contributes 250 filtered GBIF observations under the project map settings, which is enough to show that the species is established but not enough to flatten its seasonality. The densest Swedish hexes reflect where people know to search during a short spring fruiting window and where records are uploaded, not a direct measure of abundance.

notes: The map shows aggregated GBIF occurrence density rather than individual points.
Filters are restricted to HUMAN_OBSERVATION and MACHINE_OBSERVATION records from year 2000 onwards and to records with occurrenceStatus = PRESENT.
The webpage renders this layer as a hex summary map.

distribution.samplingBiasNote: GBIF density here reflects where spring fungi are actively searched for, where phone-camera observations get uploaded, and where legacy names in the Gyromitra gigas complex have already or not yet been updated. Sparse hexes can miss real populations, while dense hexes can partly reflect recorder culture and taxonomic lag rather than biology alone.

internationalContext.summary: Internationally, this species is best handled as Gyromitra gigas sensu stricto rather than as a stable old-name aggregate. Recent DOI-backed work shows that the G. gigas complex contains multiple close relatives, so range statements and older records need more caution than many familiar spring fungi do.

status.label: No global species-level IUCN assessment was confirmed during this refresh

ecology: A spring-fruiting pezizalean fungus with large folded ascomata that often appear before the main mushroom season is underway.
Swedish field sources place it on sandy soil in forest edges, clearcuts and comparable litter-rich ground, and the linked photos match that early-season substrate pattern.

Recent species-complex papers indicate that Gyromitra gigas sensu stricto is mostly European, extending into central Asia, while some morphologically similar North American records belong to other taxa.

In Swedish comparison material, the cap edge is usually freer from the stem than in stenmurkla, the flesh is paler, and full certainty can depend on microscopic spore characters rather than gross habit alone.
threats: No global Red List threat category was confirmed during this refresh.
Taxonomic lag in legacy datasets can blur the true footprint of Gyromitra gigas sensu stricto by keeping older records under broader names.
The short spring fruiting window reduces detectability in places without strong early-season fungal recording.

phenology.northernEurope: Fruiting is an early spring to early summer event, well before the main autumn mushroom season and often while the forest floor still looks winter-open.
phenology.note: This is a strong revisit species for April to early June rather than for autumn foraging walks.

swedishContext.summary: In Sweden, Artfakta/Dyntaxa accepts Gyromitra gigas and recommends blek stenmurkla as the Swedish name, while the local 2025 Red List workbook classifies it as Livskraftig (LC). The Swedish value of this species is therefore less about rarity than about timing and identification: it is an early spring storsvamp of sandy ground, skogsbryn and hyggen, and Swedish comparison sources emphasize that its cap edge is usually not fastväxt to the stem and that the odor is weak or absent compared with stenmurkla.

redList2025.documentation: De skattade värdena som bedömningen baserar sig på ligger alla inom intervallet för kategorin Livskraftig (LC).

keyFacts: Artfakta/Dyntaxa taxon 3914 treats Gyromitra gigas as accepted and blek stenmurkla as the recommended Swedish name.
The Swedish Red List 2025 workbook classifies the species as LC.
Swedish field material linked from Artfakta describes the species from sandy soil in skogsbryn and hyggen and stresses the usually free cap edge as a practical field mark.
For visitors, the main reason to return is seasonal: this fungus is easiest to catch during a short spring window when many people are not yet looking for fungi.

literature.title: Studies in Gyromitra I: the Gyromitra gigas species complex
literature.whyRelevant: Core modern paper on the species complex, useful for explaining why the focal name and several older combinations need careful synonym handling.

literature.title: Studies in Gyromitra II: cryptic speciation in the Gyromitra gigas species complex; rediscovery of G. ussuriensis and G. americanigigas sp. nov.
literature.whyRelevant: Important for current range framing because it separates Gyromitra gigas sensu stricto from cryptic relatives and places the strict species mainly in Europe and central Asia.

literature.whyRelevant: Useful for typification and diagnostic morphology in the Gyromitra gigas lineage, especially where older names and look-alikes overlap.

literature.title: A three-locus phylogeny of Gyromitra (Discinaceae, Pezizales) and discovery of two cryptic species
literature.whyRelevant: Provides broader phylogenetic context for Gyromitra and shows how quickly apparently familiar false-morel names can conceal hidden diversity.
